title: denial_validation_result.json -- denial reasons and policy links validated against case evidence v0.3
description: Produced by denial-validation's checkpoint 1. For each denial/reduction reason, validates the insurer's position against case evidence and verifies every policy match before downstream reliance.

acceptance_match_validations.description: Verification records for policy_matches owned by an accepted_coverage rather than a denial reason. Separate from `validations` because an acceptance has no insurer reasoning to rebut -- it carries no decision_type and cannot be a reason -- so it has no `verdict`, only matches needing the same verification a denial's matches get. Before this array existed, an acceptance-owned match had nowhere to go: `validations.reason_id` is `^DR_[0-9]+$`, so recording it was rejected, and omitting it raised no error at all -- the contract reported full verification while that match was never checked. Optional: a case with no accepted_coverages omits it, and every pre-2026-08-04 contract still validates.

source_denial_contract_hash.description: SHA-256 of the denial_reason_result.json this validation was built from -- specifically of the reason ids, decision types, taxonomy codes, and owned policy_match_ids it resolves against, not the whole file (an unrelated reworded summary must not invalidate a still-correct validation). The DAO recomputes this from the contract on disk at write time and refuses the write on a mismatch, so a validation of reasons that have since changed cannot be persisted. Rewriting denial_reason_result.json flips this stage back to pending in run-state rather than deleting anything.

acceptance_match_validation.description: One accepted coverage's policy-match verifications. Held to the identical standard as a denial's -- an acceptance grounded in a clause that does not exist is no better than a denial grounded that way.

policy_match_validations.description: One verification record per policy match owned by this acceptance.

verdict.description: insufficient_evidence is distinct from not_supported: the evidence contradicts the insurer's reason (not_supported) vs. there isn't enough evidence either way (insufficient_evidence, likely not rebuttal-worthy).

verdict_explanation.description: Hedged reasoning per P3 -- this is an inference, not a restatement.

retrieved_chunk_ids.description: PoC dev-phase requirement: every chunk id (from page_chunks.json) retrieval surfaced for this reason, not just what got cited below. Revisit whether this stays required post-PoC.

policy_match_validations.description: One verification record per policy match on the referenced denial reason. Empty only when that reason has no policy matches.

evidence_references.description: Final cited evidence backing the verdict. May be empty only when verdict is insufficient_evidence.

allOf.description: Rule: any verdict other than insufficient_evidence must cite at least one evidence_reference.

verification_status.description: invalid means the referenced document/clause/location is wrong or does not support the match; unverifiable means required source material is unavailable. Neither may be used as a trusted policy basis.

evidence_references.description: Source locations used to verify or reject the policy match. Verified matches require at least one.

match_source.description: Carried forward from this match's `match_source` in denial_reason_result.json, and REQUIRED here, because `verification_status: verified` is otherwise read as "the insurer's policy basis checks out" when it means only "the clause exists where the match claims it does". Those come apart completely: on CASE_909 all three matches verified byte-exact AND the insurer cited no policy clause anywhere (0 hits for 약관/보통약관/특별약관/면책/제3조/천재지변/지진/분화/홍수/해일 across all 15 pages of its response) -- its argument ran entirely on 민법 750/758조 and case law. A downstream stage that rebuts an `agent_inferred` match as though the insurer had asserted it is rebutting an argument nobody made. Duplicating the upstream field is deliberate: a consumer reading only this contract could not otherwise recover the distinction, and it had been carried in prose alone.
